code.title: The same products, easier to read.
code.description: Two invented listings, represented as JSON. Restore an omitted fact to see what changes in this scripted comparison.
code.format: Illustrative records, not an API submission format. null means the listing leaves a fact unstated.
code.questionNote: The shopper’s question sets the criteria for this comparison.
code.yourNote: Only facts already present in the sample source are restored.
code.rivalNote: The rival record stays unchanged. These are sample products, not a named brand’s catalog.
code.question: Shopper question
code.sampleNote: The code below follows question 01. The missing field is restored from the sample source; the other listing remains unchanged.

references.label: Familiar sector references
references.note: Brand examples for orientation only. No customer relationship or endorsement is implied. The sample records below are invented and unrelated to these brands.

questions.subtitle: See the question, the facts it needs and the check that still belongs to the merchant.
questions.sample: Illustrative questions; not measured search demand.

rules.models: Use ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini simulation perspectives to compare supported product facts. Perplexity currently supports Shopify referral tracking; its store simulations are coming soon. A simulation is not channel approval.

wine-and-spirits.subtitle: Make bottle facts explicit, compare the listing, and scope a purchase flow around the channel and market that permit it.
wine-and-spirits.help: Use verified origin, style, strength, price and delivery information in the comparison. Verify the source facts and permitted claims before choosing Apply, which generates and publishes the title and description. Product and destination restrictions still apply.

food-and-beverage.subtitle: Turn verified label facts into clearer product information, then review every dietary and nutrition statement before publishing.
food-and-beverage.help: Compare the ingredients, allergens, nutrition and serving information that the source actually supplies. ecentic can suggest clearer listing language; the merchant reviews claims and suitability before applying it.

beauty-and-personal-care.subtitle: Make supported ingredients and product claims easier to compare, with the evidence still attached to the source.
beauty-and-personal-care.help: Compare existing ingredients, intended use, size and supported claims. Review proposed wording against the manufacturer’s evidence; ecentic does not test efficacy or certify protection.

consumer-electronics.subtitle: Make model, compatibility and warranty information visible before a shopper reaches the store.
consumer-electronics.help: Compare the exact model and source specifications, then review suggested listing changes. Compatibility, electrical and warranty claims still need the merchant’s evidence.

home-and-furniture.subtitle: Give shoppers dimensions, materials and delivery terms they can check against their own space.
home-and-furniture.help: Compare the measurements and conditions in the source record. ecentic can expose missing listing detail; it does not guarantee fit, access or a delivery date.

fashion-and-outdoor.subtitle: Keep fit, fabric and performance descriptions tied to the product’s actual specifications.
fashion-and-outdoor.help: Compare verified sizing, materials, care and intended-use information. Review wording before publishing; ecentic does not certify technical performance or environmental claims.

health-wellness-and-pet.subtitle: Make source facts clearer without turning a product comparison into health advice.
health-wellness-and-pet.help: Compare supplied ingredients, intended use, serving or feeding information and documented standards. ecentic does not diagnose, prescribe or certify safety or health claims.

travel-and-experiences.subtitle: Make the offer’s dates, inclusions and cancellation terms explicit before the booking handoff.
travel-and-experiences.help: Compare the product information in the source. Live availability, final price and booking conditions must be confirmed with the merchant; the example is not a reservation.

bespoke.title: A custom route for age-restricted purchases.
bespoke.description: Plan an agent-assisted purchase flow with ecentic around your existing controls. Scope comes before implementation; support depends on the product, country, channel and payment provider.

steps.title: Confirm the permitted route
steps.body: Check the product, destination and chosen channel’s rules before exposing a purchase path.

steps.title: Keep the merchant’s age check
steps.body: Integrate the merchant’s existing age-verification process where required. Built-in ecentic age verification is not assumed.

steps.title: Hand over for confirmation and payment
steps.body: The buyer completes the required checks and confirms payment in the merchant’s permitted checkout flow.
